title: Gold and Silver Gift Ideas: What to Give and What to Check
summary: Looking for gold gift ideas? Here is what gift-sized gold and silver actually is, how the packaging works, and what to check before you buy a coin or bar.
body_markdown:
A gold coin gift is one of the few presents where the recipient can look up exactly what it is worth, which is either the appeal or the problem depending on who you are buying for. There is no guessing at size, no wondering whether they already own one, and nothing to assemble.


What trips people up is scale. Most gold gift ideas start and end with a one ounce bar, and one ounce of gold costs more than most people spend on a present. The useful thing to know is that gold is minted far smaller than that, and silver gets you a full-size coin for a fraction of the price.


## Can You Give a Gold or Silver Coin as a Gift?


Yes, and nothing about the transaction is unusual. You buy it, it ships to you, and you hand it over. There is no registration step, no transfer of title, and no paperwork that follows the coin.


Two practical notes. If you want it shipped somewhere other than your own address, set that at checkout rather than trying to change it after the order is placed. And if the coin is going in the mail again afterwards, keep it in the packaging it arrives in.


## What a Gift-Sized Piece Actually Is


Metal is sold by weight, so the price of any piece is mostly the price of the metal in it. That makes the arithmetic easy once you know the sizes.


**Silver, one or two ounces.** A one ounce silver coin is the standard unit. An American Silver Eagle is roughly the diameter of a silver dollar, so it reads as a real object in the hand rather than a token. Silver trades at a small fraction of gold per ounce, so this is where a modest budget buys a full-size object.


**Gold, by the gram.** This is the part that makes a gold gift work at a normal budget. Gold is minted down to a single gram, which is about one thirty-first of a troy ounce. A gram bar is smaller than a dime and costs a small fraction of what an ounce costs. Fractional coins exist too, in tenths and twentieths of an ounce.


**A certified silver dollar.** A graded Morgan dollar is a coin that circulated as money, struck from 1878 to 1904 and again in 1921, sealed by a third party with its condition assessed. It is the option with actual history attached rather than a current-year strike.


Current prices for both metals move throughout every trading day, and are benchmarked twice daily by the[LBMA](https://www.lbma.org.uk/prices-and-data/precious-metal-prices) , so the sensible move is to check the[gold](https://www.collectpure.com/charts/gold) and[silver](https://www.collectpure.com/charts/silver) charts when you are ready to buy rather than working from a figure in an article. If you want to convert between grams and ounces yourself,[what a troy ounce is](https://www.collectpure.com/blog/what-is-a-troy-ounce) covers the unit, which is heavier than the ounce on a kitchen scale.


## How the Packaging Works


This matters more for a gift than it sounds, because the packaging is most of what the recipient actually sees.


**Assay cards.** Small gold bars usually arrive sealed in a card that states the weight, the fineness, and often a serial number. The seal is part of the product: an unopened card tells any future buyer that the bar has not been swapped or altered. It presents like a document, which some people find underwhelming and others like precisely because it looks official.


**Capsules.** Bullion coins typically come in a clear plastic capsule that keeps fingerprints and air off the surface. Silver tones over time when handled, so the capsule is doing real work.


**Grading slabs.** A certified coin comes sealed in a rigid holder with its grade printed on the label, on the[1 to 70 Sheldon scale](https://www.ngccoin.com/coin-grading/grading-scale/) the grading services use. It is the largest of the three and the hardest to mistake for anything else.


None of these should be opened to inspect the contents. On a graded coin, breaking the holder removes the grade entirely.


## What to Check Before You Buy


**Weight and fineness are printed on the packaging.** Fineness is how much of the metal is the metal: .999 means 99.9% pure. Both numbers should be legible without opening anything.


**Confirm the seller has verified the item.** On Pure, every listed item has cleared a verification check and items that pass are marked Pure Qualified. We test every item ourselves to confirm the metal, and shipping is insured.


**Understand how the price was set.** Pure is a marketplace rather than a dealer, so each listing is an ask from a seller quoted against live spot for that metal. Because spot moves during the day, the same item can show a different figure in the morning and the afternoon. That is the market, not a sale.


**Give shipping room.** If a piece is going under a tree, order early enough that delivery is not the thing you are waiting on.


You can browse what is currently listed on the[marketplace](https://www.collectpure.com/marketplace) , and if you have not bought metal before,[how selling on Pure works](https://www.collectpure.com/blog/how-to-sell-on-pure-marketplace) walks through the same order book from the other side.


## Frequently Asked Questions


### Is a gold coin a good gift?


That depends entirely on the person, and it is worth being honest about the trade-offs rather than assuming. In its favor: it needs no maintenance, it does not date, it takes up no space, and the recipient can find out exactly what it is at any time. Against it: it is not personalized, it carries no sentimental content on its own, and some people would simply rather have the equivalent in something they picked out. It suits someone who already finds coins or metals interesting far better than someone who does not.


### Can we gift a gold coin to someone?


Yes. Buying a coin and giving it away involves no transfer process and no notification to anyone. Large gifts can carry tax reporting consequences for the giver depending on the amount and your situation, and that is a question for a tax professional rather than something to settle from an article.


### How much is one ounce of gold today?


It changes continuously through each trading day. The[gold chart](https://www.collectpure.com/charts/gold) shows the current spot price, and any coin or bar will be quoted at some premium above or below that, depending on the product and who is selling it.


### What size should I buy?


If you want the recipient to hold something substantial, a silver coin gift gives you the most object for the money, usually a one ounce coin. If you want it to be gold, a gram bar is the smallest piece that still arrives properly sealed and identified. If you want it to have history, a certified silver dollar is the one that circulated.


### Does the recipient need to do anything with it?


No. A coin in a capsule or a bar in a sealed assay card needs no special storage and no upkeep. A drawer is fine. The weight and fineness are printed on the packaging, so the information travels with the object.


### How much silver is in an older silver coin?


It depends on the coin. A Morgan dollar holds 0.7734 troy ounces, and[we work through that calculation](https://www.collectpure.com/blog/how-much-silver-is-in-a-morgan-silver-dollar) including how to check a coin by weight. Pre-1965 dimes, quarters and half dollars are 90% silver and are priced by face value rather than per coin, which[how to sell junk silver coins](https://www.collectpure.com/blog/how-to-sell-junk-silver) covers.
